In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single method for producing a reliable amplitude estimate of surface electromyography that will work in all situations.

the best EMG amplitude estimate is obtained by the use of a well designed active electrode system, a well designed signal recording system, and a signal processing algorithm that includes all of the above stages.
the current state-of-the-art for surface EMG amplitude estimation is still in its infancy and much work remains to be done before the full potential of this technique will be realized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amplitude of EMG can be estimated with high accuracy and reliability, provided the signal is recorded from well prepared skin and with high quality active electrodes and recording instrumentation.
we have developed a method for estimating the amplitude envelope of surface EMG that is based on a model of the underlying muscle fibre action potential.
there is no single best method for reducing noise or estimating the amplitude of surface EMG, rather the choice of method is dependent upon the specific requirements of each application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amplitude of the surface EMG signal is a complex function of the underlying muscle activity, the skin-electrode impedance, and the electrode-skin contact area.
there is a clear need for a more comprehensive and standardized approach to EMG data acquisition, processing and analysis.
